beats.html:
Today
How to buy a business with no money down.

It applies whether
1It's your first business or your next
2You have money or you don't

Josh, his clients, his network
From the $1M business to the $100M business.

First principles
Buy something without the thing required to buy it.

Three things
1You
2The money
3The business you want

If you don't have the money
Use other people's money.

The simplest form
Borrow it: investors and lenders.

Josh prefers lending, because investors mean
1Giving up equity
2Someone else's oversight

If you want to run your own company
The investor route's probably not the play.

Lending
You don't dilute yourself.

The bank
1Gives you the money
2Charges interest
3Gets paid back monthly

Remember
The bank isn't a manager. It's your debt owner.

Option three · Josh's favourite
Borrow from the vendor.

His clinic deal
A double layer: vendor finance + commercial lending.
The full template is in the Owners Academy community.

Vendor finance
Basically an IOU to the seller.

The pitch
"I'll pay what you want, plus more, over time."

The reality for sellers
1No one's paying the price they want
25–10 years hunting a unicorn buyer
3Then shut down with nothing

Many owners know it
Something over time beats nothing.

A true story
Josh followed up with an owner for years.

One day, driving past
The clinic was dark. "Closed."

The clinic
The pinnacle of a private allied health clinic.

Long story short
No deal. He had to liquidate.

Josh shared that story with
Another owner who wants to sell, doesn't want to sell.

Why vendor finance works
Sellers get what they deserve, over time.

Three ways to fund a deal
1Investor
2Lender
3Vendor

Then the real question
Can you run it?

That's why Josh says
Look for $1M+ revenue: management and systems in place.

No experience?
Same as the money: use other people.

Borrow their
1Credibility
2Capabilities
3Expertise

JC Health Group
Josh had never worked in healthcare.

So he built a board
1National CEOs of healthcare companies
2Legal
3Finance

The board
Helped him do and run his first deal.
Today they're his advisors.

An entrepreneur
Creates something from nothing.

You can't do it the conventional way
Get creative. Test the market.

Josh's mistakes
Every one of them benefited him.

The lesson
Grow some scar tissue. Learn to detach.

How Josh got into healthcare
Bought his first clinic. Built a multi-million dollar company.

No cookie-cutter answer
Follow the principles.
